question: What is the primary difference between a perineal laceration and an episiotomy?

options.A: A laceration requires immediate suturing whereas an episiotomy is left to heal naturally
options.B: An episiotomy is caused by forceps use while a laceration results from rapid pushing
options.C: An episiotomy occurs only in the cervix while a laceration affects the perineal skin
options.D: A laceration is a jagged spontaneous tear while an episiotomy is a planned surgical cut

explanation: Spontaneous tears present with irregular edges caused by tissue stretching, whereas episiotomies involve deliberate surgical incisions. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h1)

question: Where is the perineum located on the female anatomy?

options.A: Inside the upper third of the vaginal canal
options.B: Between the vaginal opening and the anus
options.C: Between the clitoris and the urethral meatus
options.D: Directly above the pubic symphysis bone

explanation: The perineum forms the muscular floor structure spanning the space separating the lower vagina and the anal sphincter. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h1)

question: Which structure serves as the central tendon where multiple perineal muscles converge?
explanation: The perineal body anchors several pelvic floor muscles and acts as the structural keystone of the perineum. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h2)

question: Why must pelvic floor muscles undergo extreme stretching during normal vaginal delivery?

options.A: To allow the passage of the foetal head through the birth canal
options.B: To prevent the amniotic fluid from escaping prematurely
options.C: To widen the pelvis permanently for future pregnancies
options.D: To release hormones that stimulate postpartum uterine contractions

explanation: The pelvic floor muscles distend widely to let the baby descend through the lower reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h2)

question: A tear involving the perineal skin and vaginal mucosa without muscle injury is classified as what degree?
explanation: First-degree tears are superficial, affecting only the skin and mucous membranes without damaging underlying muscles. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h3)

question: A patient diagnosed with a fourth-degree perineal tear has damage to which additional structure not affected in a second-degree tear?
explanation: Fourth-degree tears extend through the anal sphincter complex to involve the mucous membrane lining the rectum. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a known risk factor for severe perineal lacerations?

options.A: Rapid, unmanaged second stage of labour
options.B: Foetal birth weight over four kilograms
options.C: Use of forceps during second stage

explanation: Having previous vaginal births typically stretches and conditions the perineal tissues, lowering the risk of severe tears compared to nulliparity. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h4)

question: A primigravida is pushing intensely with a large baby and a rigid perineum. What complication is she most at risk for?
explanation: First-time mothers with large babies and firm tissues face high mechanical strain, frequently resulting in perineal tears. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h4)

question: Why is a digital rectal examination performed as part of routine postpartum perineal assessment?

options.A: To check for hidden damage to the anal sphincter muscles
options.B: To measure the exact depth of vaginal mucosal tears
options.C: To clear retained lochia from the lower rectal vault
options.D: To stimulate uterine contraction and prevent heavy bleeding

explanation: A rectal exam allows the midwife to palpate the sphincter and detect third- or fourth-degree injuries that are not visible externally. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h5)

question: When is the best time to perform the initial genital tract inspection for lacerations?

options.A: Immediately after the delivery of the placenta
options.B: Twenty-four hours after the birth process
options.C: Right when the second stage of labour begins
options.D: Before the baby is weighed and measured

explanation: Inspecting the birth canal right after placental delivery ensures prompt identification and repair of any sustained injuries. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for prompt repair of a postpartum perineal laceration?

options.A: To speed up the involution of the postpartum uterus
options.B: To prevent the development of postpartum depression
options.C: To reduce blood loss and minimize the risk of infection
options.D: To ensure the mother can breastfeed immediately without pain

explanation: Timely suturing stops bleeding vessels and closes open tissue planes where bacteria can easily multiply. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h6)

question: Why is anatomical alignment emphasized when a midwife sutures a deep perineal tear?

options.A: To ensure the external skin looks cosmetically smooth
options.B: To restore normal function and prevent long-term incontinence
options.C: To shorten the duration of the lochia discharge period
options.D: To make future vaginal examinations completely painless

explanation: Accurately matching muscle layers, especially the sphincter, prevents complications like flatal or faecal incontinence later in life. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of applying cold packs to the perineum shortly after repair?

options.A: To reduce swelling and numb nerve pain
options.B: To speed up the absorption of surgical sutures
options.C: To increase local blood flow to the wound
options.D: To stimulate early contraction of the bladder

explanation: Cold therapy causes vasoconstriction which decreases oedema and provides a soothing local anesthetic effect on traumatized tissue. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h7)

question: Why is cleaning the perineal area from front to back emphasized for postpartum women?

options.A: To encourage normal urinary voiding reflexes after birth
options.B: To prevent the transfer of bacteria from the anal region
options.C: To ensure all lochia is pushed directly into the vaginal canal
options.D: To avoid putting direct pressure on the newly tied knots

explanation: Wiping from front to back stops fecal bacteria from contaminating the perineal wound and causing infection. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h7)

question: What is a common long-term sexual complication linked to poorly healed perineal tears?
explanation: Scar tissue formation and improper alignment from poor repair frequently cause painful intercourse, known medically as dyspareunia. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h8)

question: What primary problem arises when a deep perineal hematoma develops under a sutured laceration?

options.B: Rapid healing of the underlying fascia

explanation: Bleeding beneath the closed skin forms a trapped pool of blood that stretches tissues, causing intense throbbing pain. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h8)
